LanguageData.RP_DrugTestDesc:
Whether a doctor tests inmates for drugs. Targeted tests an inmate after a contraband find on them or in their cell, a tip naming them, an overdose they survived, and in the two days before the inmate's next parole hearing or trial (each reason at most once in two days, a hearing or a trial once). Targeted and random adds a few inmates picked at random each day, and being searched again wears on the tempers of those picked.
A doctor of the day shift takes the inmate aside for about {0} ticks and uses up a drug test kit (bought through the supply company). Never the night doctor, never the only doctor on site, and no more than {1} tests an hour in the prison. An inmate in the hole, in supermax, in a hostage situation, a riot, a class or at an appointment is tested at the next hour.
A positive is a drug used in the last two days. It means a seen drug use on the record (confinement to the cell by default), a referral to substance abuse treatment, lower parole odds and, for a customer of a dealer, the chance to trace the dealer. An addiction with no use in the last two days is a positive for dependence - the referral, the file line and the parole odds, but no misconduct and no punishment. A refusal is a seen misconduct of its own (four hours in the hole by default) and, like a positive, counts against them with the parole board for five days. A riot or a hostage situation stops the round at once.
